name: Air Fryers
hub_intro: The air fryer conquered the Irish kitchen for one simple reason: with electricity prices among Europe's highest, heating a whole oven to cook for two people stopped making sense. A typical air fryer uses 50–70% less energy than a conventional oven for everyday meals — and does chips better. We compare every size and budget, from compact singles to dual-drawer family machines.
guide: 1–2 people: 3.5–5L. Families of 3–4: 6–8L or dual-zone. Batch cookers and big families: 9L+. Under-buying is the #1 regret in reviews — a too-small basket means cooking in frustrating rounds.

Two drawers let you cook mains and sides simultaneously at different temperatures — the feature families keep once they've had it. Singles are cheaper, smaller on the counter, and fine for one or two people.

An air fryer at ~1,500 W cooking for 20 minutes uses roughly 0.5 kWh (~18 cents). A fan oven preheated and run for 45 minutes uses 1.3–1.8 kWh (~45–65 cents). Cook five times a week and the machine pays for itself within a year or two.

Skip the 12-preset marketing. What separates good from bad: drawer build quality, even cooking without shaking religiously, dishwasher-safe parts, and a max temp of 200°C+. Ninja dominates because it nails these four.

faqs.q: Do air fryers really save money in Ireland?
faqs.a: Yes, meaningfully. Cooking a typical meal costs ~15–20 cents in an air fryer versus 45–65 cents in a fan oven at current rates. A family cooking five evenings a week saves roughly €80–120 a year — most machines pay for themselves inside 18 months.

faqs.q: What size air fryer should I buy?
faqs.a: 3.5–5L for one or two people, 6–8L (or a dual-drawer) for a family of four, 9L+ for batch cooking. When in doubt, size up: the most common review complaint is a basket too small for a full family dinner.

faqs.q: Is a dual-zone air fryer worth it?
faqs.a: For families, yes — cooking chicken in one drawer and chips in the other, finishing together, removes the juggling that makes weeknight cooking stressful. For one or two people a quality single drawer is better value and counter space.

faqs.q: Ninja vs Tower vs Tefal — which brand?
faqs.a: Ninja leads on build quality, even cooking and resale value, at a price premium. Tower undercuts everyone with respectable quality. Tefal sits between, strong on capacity innovation. Our testing-based view: buy Ninja if budget allows, Tower if it doesn't.

faqs.q: Can an air fryer replace my oven?
faqs.a: For most weeknight cooking — chips, chicken, fish, roast veg, reheating — completely. You'll still want the oven for large roasts, multiple trays of baking, or pizza. Many Irish households now use the big oven once or twice a week at most.

faqs.q: How much electricity does an air fryer use?
faqs.a: Typical units draw 1,400–2,400 W but only heat intermittently. A 20-minute cook uses about 0.4–0.6 kWh — 15–22 cents at standard Irish rates. Night-rate owners on smart meters can batch-cook even cheaper.

They achieve fried texture with 70–90% less oil than deep frying, cutting calories and acrylamide exposure versus a chip pan. They're a cooking method, not a health product — but replacing deep-fried food with air-fried is a clear nutritional win.

faqs.q: What can't an air fryer do?
faqs.a: Anything with wet batter (it drips before setting), very large roasts, and big baking trays. Steaks are better in a pan. Everything else from frozen chips to whole chickens (in 7L+ models) is fair game.

pages.title: 5 Best Air Fryers in Ireland 2026 — Tested & Compared
pages.desc: Ireland's best air fryers compared on cooking quality, energy savings at Irish electricity rates, capacity and value. Top 5 for 2026.
pages.h1: The 5 Best Air Fryers in Ireland (2026)
pages.intro: Half of Irish kitchens now have an air fryer; the other half are deciding which one. We compared the bestsellers on the things that matter after the honeymoon: even cooking without constant shaking, drawers that survive the dishwasher, capacity honesty, and energy use at Irish rates. Five machines stood out across budgets from €70 to €270.

products.name: Ninja Air Fryer MAX PRO 6.2L (AF180UK)
pros: Crispiest results of anything we compared
products.verdict: The best single-drawer air fryer on the Irish market: enough capacity for a small family, even cooking that doesn't demand babysitting, and Ninja durability.

products.name: Ninja Foodi Dual Zone 7.6L (AF300UK)
pros: The most-loved kitchen gadget in Ireland, justifiably
products.verdict: The family dinner machine. Chicken in drawer one, chips in drawer two, both ready at once — weeknight cooking permanently simplified.

products.name: Tower Vortx 4L (T17087)
cons: Needs a mid-cook shake for even results
products.verdict: The honest cheap option: less refined than Ninja but the chips don't know that. Perfect first air fryer for singles, couples and students.

products.name: Tefal Easy Fry Dual XXL 11L (EY942BG0)
products.verdict: The big-family answer: whole-household dinners in one go at a price Ninja can't match per litre. Bring a tape measure for your counter first.

products.name: Philips 3000 Series Airfryer L (NA231/00)
pros: RapidAir = least shaking required of any unit
products.verdict: From the company that invented the category: the most forgiving air fryer for people who want to set, walk away, and not shake baskets.

pages.title: Best Air Fryers Under €100 in Ireland 2026 — Top 5 Cheap Picks
pages.desc: Five air fryers under €100 that actually cook well — compared on results, capacity and warranty for Irish budgets in 2026.
pages.h1: Best Air Fryers Under €100 in Ireland
pages.intro: Under €100 is where most first air fryers are bought — and where the gap between 'cheap and good' and 'cheap and disposable' is widest. The five below all crisp properly and carry real warranties; the differences are capacity, controls and how much shaking the basket demands. One of them embarrasses machines twice its price.

products.name: Tower Vortx 4L (T17087)
pros: Reliable crisping at a giveaway price
products.verdict: The default budget buy. Tower has quietly become the value king of UK-Irish kitchens, and the 3-year warranty shows their confidence.

products.name: COSORI 4.7L Pro LE
pros: Square basket fits more than round rivals
products.verdict: The internet's favourite budget air fryer for a reason: 90% of the Ninja experience at 55% of the price. Our pick if you can stretch to €89.

products.name: Salter EK4548 XL 8L
pros: Viewing window — rare at this price
cons: Less even than smaller units; rotate food
products.verdict: Feeds a family of four for the price of a single-drawer toy. Demands a little more technique (rotate halfway) but the value is undeniable.

products.name: Russell Hobbs SatisFry Air 5L
pros: 5L hits the couple/small family sweet spot
products.verdict: The comfortable choice: familiar brand, sensible size, frequent discounts. Watch for it under €65 — at that price it outvalues everything here.

products.name: Ninja Air Fryer 3.8L (AF100UK)
pros: Compact yet fits a 1.4 kg chicken
Best resale value in the category
products.verdict: The entry ticket to the best brand in the category. Couples who value cooking quality over capacity should spend their €99 here.

pages.title: Best Dual Zone Air Fryers Ireland 2026 — Ninja vs Tefal vs Tower
pages.desc: Dual-drawer air fryers compared for Irish families: Ninja, Tefal, Tower and more on sync cooking, capacity and value. Top 5 for 2026.
pages.h1: Best Dual Zone Air Fryers in Ireland
pages.intro: Dual-zone is the air fryer feature with the highest keep-rate: once a family cooks mains and sides simultaneously with both finishing together, there's no going back to juggling. Ninja invented the category and still leads it, but Tefal and Tower now attack on capacity and price. We compared the five dual-drawer machines worth Irish counter space.

products.name: Ninja Foodi Dual Zone 7.6L (AF300UK)
pros: The original and still the benchmark
products.verdict: Ireland's favourite kitchen appliance, full stop. Every rival is measured against this — and none has beaten it on overall cooking quality yet.

products.name: Ninja Double Stack XL 9.5L (SL400UK)
pros: Vertical design: more litres, half the width
products.verdict: Ninja's answer to the only complaint about the AF300: width. More capacity on a footprint the size of a kettle zone — galley-kitchen families, this is yours.

products.name: Tefal Easy Fry Dual XXL 11L (EY942BG0)
products.verdict: The rational family pick: 45% more capacity than the AF300 for less money. If your priority is feeding a crowd rather than perfect chip edges, Tefal wins.

products.name: Tower Vortx Eco Dual Drawer 8.5L
products.verdict: Dual drawers for half Ninja money. You lose the sync magic and some refinement; you keep the core trick of two simultaneous dishes. Fair trade at €109.

products.name: Instant Vortex Plus VersaZone 8.5L
pros: Whole chicken AND dual-zone in one machine
cons: Single heating element splits power in dual mode
products.verdict: The transformer: a big single-basket machine on Sunday, a dual-zone on Tuesday. No rival offers both shapes — flexibility seekers look no further.

pages.title: Best Large Air Fryers for Big Families Ireland 2026 (9L+)
pages.desc: Feeding 5+ people? The best large-capacity 9L+ air fryers and multi-cookers in Ireland compared on real capacity and value. Top 5.
pages.h1: Best Large Air Fryers for Big Families in Ireland
pages.intro: For households of five-plus, most 'family' air fryers still mean cooking in rounds while someone's chips go cold. True big-family machines start at 9 litres and climb to oven-replacing 15L multi-cookers. We compared honest usable capacity — not marketing litres — plus whether each can handle a whole chicken, a full bag of frozen chips, or both at once.

products.name: Ninja Double Stack XL 9.5L (SL400UK)
pros: Four food layers possible at once
products.verdict: The big-family machine that respects your kitchen: four portions of mains plus two sides in one cycle, on a footprint narrower than a microwave.

products.name: Tefal Easy Fry Dual XXL 11L
pros: Each zone fits a family side dish
products.verdict: Maximum litres per euro in the large class. For families who want big and simple — two huge drawers, no racks, no fuss — Tefal owns this slot.

products.name: Ninja Foodi MAX 15-in-1 SmartLid 7.5L
pros: Pressure-cooks AND air-crisps a whole chicken
Probe takes guesswork out of roasts
products.verdict: For families whose bottleneck is time, not just capacity: pressure-cook a roast in 25 minutes, crisp the skin in 10. Sunday dinner, weeknight schedule.

products.name: Salter Fuzion Dual 9L
cons: Crisping needs a shake or two
products.verdict: The budget route to feeding five: 90% of the Tefal's capacity for 75% of its price. Set two timers, give it a shake, dinner's done.

products.name: Tower Vortx Vizion 14L Air Fryer Oven
pros: Three flat racks suit pizzas and trays
cons: Oven format crisps slower than drawers
products.verdict: Half air fryer, half mini-oven: trays, rotisserie and visibility that drawer machines can't offer. Best for families who bake and roast more than they chip.

pages.title: Best Compact Air Fryers for Small Kitchens Ireland 2026
pages.desc: Small air fryers for apartments, small kitchens and singles in Ireland — compact footprints, real capacity, low energy. Top 5 compared.
pages.h1: Best Compact Air Fryers for Small Kitchens in Ireland
pages.intro: Apartment kitchens — and Ireland builds a lot of them now — force a question the air fryer industry ignores: what fits? A machine can be brilliant and still useless if it can't live on your counter. These five deliver real air-fried results from footprints smaller than a sheet of A4 (well, nearly), ranked on cooking quality per square centimetre.

products.name: Ninja Air Fryer 3.8L (AF100UK)
pros: Full Ninja quality, two-thirds the size
Still fits a small whole chicken
cons: Couples cooking big portions will feel limits
products.verdict: The compact machine that doesn't cook like one. If only one air fryer fits your kitchen, make it the one with the best brand behind it.

products.name: COSORI Mini 2.1L
cons: One portion at a time, really
products.verdict: The studio-apartment special: dinner for one, snacks for two, counter space for everything else. The smallest air fryer that still does the job properly.

products.name: Tower Vortx Compact 2.2L
pros: Tiny and light — moves to a cupboard easily
products.verdict: The toe-in-the-water buy: students, singles and the air-fryer-curious get the real experience for the price of a takeaway week.

products.name: Philips 1000 Series 4.2L (NA120/00)
pros: 4.2L squeezed into a slim vertical body
products.verdict: The clever shape: family-adjacent capacity on a single-person footprint by building up, not out. Narrow counters, meet your match.

products.name: Instant Vortex Slim 5.7L
pros: Genuine family capability in slim form
products.verdict: The capacity magician of the compact class: small-family portions from a body that slots beside the kettle. The spec-per-centimetre winner.
